accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to as male throughout ("his uncle", "he").

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is stated.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community is named.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No wealth or class statement about the accused appears.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: Victim is Makhan Singh, the accused's male uncle.

victim_age.reason: Only "old and feeble man" is stated; no age in years.

victim_caste.reason: No caste of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religion of the victim is stated.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Nephew-uncle relationship and the previous day's quarrel are both described.

offence_category.reason: Final conviction is culpable homicide not amounting to murder under s.304 Part II.

statutory_provisions.reason: Charge under s.302 IPC and final conviction under s.304 Part II IPC are both supported.

weapon.reason: Wooden 'Bahi', the side of a cot frame, is the weapon described.

evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, medical and recovery evidence are all relied upon.

confession.correct_value: Accused's confession/disclosure of where the 'Bahi' was hidden, leading to its recovery; relied on by the Supreme Court
confession.quote: the recovery ... was recovered by police only after the appellant had confessed about the place of hiding
confession.reason: Confession and reliance are supported, but the judgment never says the disclosure was police-recorded.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: High Court noted great force, skull fracture, feeble victim and grudge; all supported.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: Provocation, non-dangerous weapon, single blow and lack of intention or knowledge are all noted.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Acquittal on 13.07.2001 with the listed reasons is supported.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court set aside acquittal, convicted under s.302, life imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine, 03.04.2014.

final_outcome.reason: Conviction altered to s.304 Part II, so conviction_modified is right.

offence_finally_established.reason: Final conviction is under s.304 Part II IPC.

imprisonment_type.correct_value: fixed_term (sentence reduced to period already undergone; no number of years stated)
imprisonment_type.quote: His sentence shall be reduced from life imprisonment to period already undergone.
imprisonment_type.reason: Sentence is 'period already undergone', not a stated fixed term; the type label is debatable.

imprisonment_years.reason: No number of years is stated, so null is consistent with the judgment.

fine_rs.reason: Rs.5,000 fine retained as imposed by the High Court.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Same factual summary, using gender-neutral references (e.g. 'the accused' and 'the victim') instead of he/him/his
neutral_facts.quote: threatened to teach Makhan Singh a lesson
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate and stay within the incident, but gendered pronouns (he/him/his) breach the no-pronoun rule.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment does not state the statutory punishment prescribed for s.302 or s.304.

attempt_completion.reason: Death resulted, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.reason: Single head blow, skull fracture, eight injuries and death next day are all stated.

number_of_offences.reason: One charge (s.302) and one final conviction (s.304 Part II).

financial_property_loss.reason: No property or money loss is discussed.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Not expressly addressed by the Supreme Court; no premeditation finding recorded
premeditation_planning.quote: the occurrence had not taken place all of a sudden and without any predetermination
premeditation_planning.reason: The 'not sudden/no predetermination' point is the High Court's; the Supreme Court never addressed premeditation expressly.

motive.reason: Court accepted fury and provocation from the previous day's reprimand as the motive.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Eyewitness accounts, post-mortem and recovery with chemical match were relied upon.

witness_credibility.reason: High Court found ocular version truthful; Supreme Court accepted occurrence proved beyond reasonable doubt.

post_offence_conduct.reason: Fled with the weapon, concealed it at home, arrested 09.08.1998, and disclosure led to recovery.

custody_duration.reason: Arrest, release after acquittal, surrender and over eight years' incarceration are all stated.

bail_history.reason: No bail grant or refusal is stated; release followed the acquittal.

trial_duration.reason: Incident, trial order, High Court and Supreme Court dates all match the judgment.

legal_representation.reason: Gagan Gupta for appellant; R.K. Rathore and Ms. Jaspreet Gogia for respondents.

investigation_status.reason: FIR, site visit, inquest, arrest, recovery, committal, charge and trial are all described.

procedural_irregularity.reason: Trial court's FIR delay and late-arrest concerns are noted; no separate Supreme Court irregularity appears.

appeal_history.reason: Trial acquittal, High Court conviction under s.302, and Supreme Court partial allowance are all accurate.

prosecution_argument.reason: No prosecution arguments before the Supreme Court are recorded.

defence_argument.reason: Alternative plea of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under s.304 is recorded.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Intention, knowledge and degree of act, with Pulicherla factors, are the principles applied.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Mohd. Rafiq with its quoted Rayavarapu Punnayya and Pulicherla Nagaraju passages is relied upon.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Lack of intention and knowledge, plus over eight years served, are the stated reasons.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No intention, provocation, non-dangerous weapon, single blow, no knowledge and time served are weighed.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The Supreme Court weighs no aggravating factors itself.

other_sentence_order.reason: Release forthwith if not wanted elsewhere; fine remains at Rs.5,000.
